post.description:
Move businesses with no subscription onto a plan without charging them (free trial or complimentary). Dry run by
default; a real run needs the exact count from the preview.

get.description: The inbox. People with approval authority (or approvals:read) see every request; everyone else sees only their own.
Credit sales held because they went over the credit limit. They are decided with the existing order approve / reject actions.
Active plans with their current prices and entitlements. Public, cached for a couple of minutes.

How much each core module is actually being used, for all businesses or for the group the filters select:
adoption (businesses with at least one record) and volume (total records).
Breakdown charts: country, industry, business_type, heard_about, status, plan, monthly signups.

Deep-dive into how tenants actually use the platform: engagement tiers
(by order volume), per-plan usage (users, orders, revenue, products) and
the top tenants by order count. All aggregate queries — one grouped query
per metric, never one per tenant — matching the /stats and /feature-usage
approach so it stays cheap regardless of tenant count.

post.description:
Superadmin-only (enforced by the `SuperUser` dependency server-side,
not just a hidden frontend button). Builds the export from exactly the
same filtered query the dashboard list uses — see
_build_admin_users_query — so "Filtered Results" always matches what's
on screen, at any size, without paging through the frontend.

get.description:
Market-research figures for the businesses the filters select: how many, how fast they join, what they are like, and whether they use the product.
Archived businesses never count (they are not part of the market).
Every value a business can be filtered by, with how many businesses have it.

Contactable businesses for marketing: one row per business with its owner's name/email and the business phone.
Platform-staff only. Archived businesses never appear; owners come from the earliest active owner user.
Branches and warehouses of one business with their real counts: users and warehouses per branch, products, units and stock value per warehouse (from the stock ledger).
Read-only, paginated business records for the selected tenant.

The four headline KPIs with a previous-period comparison. Honours the
date range and every tenant filter. Four aggregate queries, run concurrently.

New vs running-total tenants or users per bucket. Honours the date range
and every tenant filter; the running total starts from everything created
before the range so the line is the true total, not just the window's.

Tenant status mix right now (tenant filters apply; the date range does
not — status has no history) plus a live database round-trip, the only
system-health signal the backend can truthfully report.

Top categories (+ rolled-up "Other") of one signup dimension among
tenants registered in the period. Honours the date range and the tenant
filters *except the one for this dimension*: a "by country" breakdown with
Country = Rwanda selected would only ever say "Rwanda 100%", so that one
filter is ignored here (and flagged via `ignoredFilter`).
'View all' drill-down: the full, paginated category list for one dimension.

The newest registrations. Honours the tenant filters; not the date range —
"recent" means the latest joiners, not those inside an arbitrary window.

Values for the Country / Industry / Business Type dropdowns, straight
from the tenants table so new values appear automatically.

post.description: Email the user a time-limited reset link. The admin never sees a password or the link.

Give any user in any business a password you choose (a default for them to sign in with). By default they must choose their own
at the next sign-in. The password itself is never written to the audit log or returned.

patch.description: Edit a catalogue entry. The key never changes and nothing a business has recorded is touched.

put.description: Whether the administrator who requested an operation may also approve it. Changing it needs the approval permission and is audited.

get.description: Real numbers for the Data Management overview. A figure that cannot be worked out is null, never invented.
Businesses to choose from, filtered, sorted and paged on the server. Nothing about a business's records is shown until it is chosen.
The checklist of Reset Business Data: every data group with its live record count for this business, the presets and what is always kept.

post.description: A short-lived download link for the backup a data reset took before it deleted anything.

get.description: What the business recorded on one calendar day (in its own time zone), module by module: the starting point of Reset Business Day.

post.description: Stage A: work out exactly what the operation would do. Changes nothing.
Stage B: re-check everything and run. Running an operation that already ran returns its result and does nothing more.
Submit, approve and run in one step for the requester, while the platform allows self-approval. Everything is checked again before it runs.

get.description: What can really be recovered. There is no backup system in this platform, so this says so rather than listing restore points that do not exist.

Acquisition dashboard: visitors → signups → activated → paying, with sources, pages and campaigns.
Platform-wide (never tenant-scoped); superadmin only.
Visitors on the website right now (last 30 minutes) and the last 48 hours, hour by hour. Superadmin only.
Every channel with views, signups and conversion, a per-channel trend, and the top referring sites.
Every tracked page (up to 500) with visitors, views and the signups credited to it as a landing page.
Every UTM campaign with its source/medium breakdown, signups and paying customers.
How businesses use the ERP: active users/businesses, sessions, modules, most active and quiet businesses.

post.description: Anonymous page-view beacon from the marketing website. Invalid or bot traffic is ignored silently.
Page-view beacon from the signed-in ERP/POS. Platform staff (no business) and malformed input are ignored.

get.description: Contact directory. Syncs businesses into contacts first, so it always reflects the current tenant list.
Values for the filter drop-downs: only what exists in the data.
A contact's profile: the business, its authorised recipient, preferences and message history.

post.description: The exact HTML and plain text recipients get, with sample data in the variables.
Stores an email image in the shared uploads folder (served at /uploads) after verifying it really is an image.
Signs in to the SMTP server without sending anything.

get.description: Shows a confirm button: merely opening the link (a mail scanner, a preview) never unsubscribes anyone.

post.description: Also the RFC 8058 one-click target (mail apps POST here directly).

put.description: Changes how cross-tenant analytics are presented. Does not touch any tenant's base currency.

get.description: Dashboard insights: verified calculations only (no model call), cached for a few minutes.

post.description: The ONLY place an AI-prepared draft becomes a real record. Re-validates permission, prices and rules.

put.description:
Feature switch + usage limits. The provider and its API key are deployment configuration
(environment variables), deliberately not editable — or readable — through the app.

get.description:
The business's base (accounting) currency and whether it can still be changed — it is frozen
as soon as any transaction exists, so the UI can disable the control and say why.
The rate a new document would get: `from` → `to` (default: the tenant's base currency), as of `at`.
Right-hand customer panel: previous conversations with the same person and their tickets.
Staff can open attachments of conversations they may see; a business user only attachments on THEIR OWN tickets.
Channel status for the Settings page. Only non-secret state — never keys, tokens or session data.

post.description: Signs in to SMTP and Graph without sending anything. Reports ok/error per direction — never credentials.
Starts a separate conversation with each chosen business and sends the message on the chosen channel.

get.description: Server-Sent Events: instant 'something changed' nudges for the open inbox (no polling).

schema.description: Filter batches expiring within N days
schema.title: Expiring In Days

parameters.description: Filter batches expiring within N days

get.description: How many products are in each VAT treatment, including those not reviewed yet.

post.description: Bulk VAT classification. Needs tax:update (owners and administrators always may).
A ZIP of pictures named after each product's SKU or barcode. Pictures that match are attached; the rest are listed with the reason.
Pictures pasted into an import sheet, attached to the products just created from its rows. `rows` is JSON {sheet row: product id}.

get.description: Every active branch of the business, by name only: a branch-restricted person may send stock TO any branch.

post.description: Switch warehouses on for the business: creates the Main warehouse holding everything now in stock.

get.description:
Customers, without archived ones unless asked (status). figures=true adds each customer's orders, completed sales,
last order and unpaid balance, aggregated in one query for the page.

delete.description:
Permanent deletion: owners/administrators only (enforced by the access layer), and refused while any sale, payment,
debt, quotation or other record refers to the customer.

get.description: What refers to the customer, so the screen can say why deletion is unavailable before anyone tries.
What happened to this customer record (created, edited, deactivated, archived, reactivated), from the audit log.

post.description: Deactivate, archive or reactivate (contacts:update). History, debts and journals are never touched.

get.description: The VAT the business really charges, so the till shows what the server will record (never a hard-coded rate).

post.description:
VAT for a cart before it is charged, from the same engine the checkout uses (read-only, nothing is stored).
The till shows these figures, so it never charges a total the server would not record.

get.description: Active people who can be named as the salesperson on a sale (names only: it needs no access to user administration).

patch.description: Re-credit a sale to another salesperson. Needs approval authority on sales; the reason is audited.

get.description: The receipt at the paper it will be printed on: 80 mm / 58 mm thermal rolls, or an A4 sheet.

post.description: Owner/administrator correction of a completed sale: reverses the old books entry and posts a new one. Never edits in place.
Owner/administrator: cancel a completed sale that should not exist. Reverses its entries and payments and restores stock; deletes nothing.
Anyone who can see a sale can ask for it to be voided; an owner or approver decides in Approvals.
Accepted quotation -> one Pending sale. Repeating the call returns the same sale. Takes no payment and moves no stock.
Create accounting transactions for all completed orders that don't have one yet.

get.description: Output VAT by treatment, input VAT, returns and the net VAT position, reconciled to the ledger (tax:read).
Get reference Rwanda tax rates

post.description: Calculate PAYE for a given salary
Calculate VAT for a given amount
Calculate withholding tax
Calculate pension contributions
Calculate corporate income tax
Calculate consumption tax

get.description: List all tax configurations

post.description: Create a tax configuration

get.description: List tax calculations

post.description: Create a tax calculation record

get.description: Get tax summary for a period
List tax payments

post.description: Record a tax payment

get.description: One day for one branch (or all the person's branches): sales per item, debt, deposits, stock movement and expenses.
KPIs, trend, breakdowns and insights for any period, optionally compared with another period.
Sales per salesperson with the orders behind every figure. Without team access you only see yourself.
The directory: every branch the person may see with staff and sales for the chosen period, in a handful of grouped queries.
One branch's sales for a period against the period before it, with trend, top products, payment methods and recent orders.
Recorded changes to this branch: created, edited, activated or deactivated, made main, deleted.
Which roles can use one module and what changed about it. Visible to anyone who can read roles.
Roles that can delete or approve, and how many people hold each, so an owner can decide whether to tighten them.

post.description: Owner-initiated: remove delete and approve from the built-in Member role. Never runs automatically.
Adds the built-in roles this business doesn't have yet (Branch Manager, Cashier ...). Roles it already has are left exactly as they are.

patch.description:
Self-service. Ungated so any signed-in user can fix their own name and
phone; MyProfileUpdate keeps role/status/email off-limits. Declared before
the `/{user_id}` routes so the literal path can't be shadowed.

post.description:
Self-service. Deliberately ungated by `users:update` — every user
must be able to change their own password. Declared before the
`/{user_id}` routes so the literal path can never be shadowed by a path
parameter.

get.description:
Audit trail for one user: the actions they performed plus every admin
action taken against their account.

post.description:
Sets the password the administrator chose, or generates one, and emails it to the user. A generated value is
never returned to the caller.

get.description: Effective feature flags + usage limits for the current tenant.
The plan and every module's state for the signed-in business (see service.resolve_modules).

patch.description: The business administrator turns a module their plan includes on or off. Data is never deleted.

get.description:
Real, safe-to-publish numbers for the marketing site. No auth — this
is meant to be fetched from public pages — so it must never include
per-tenant data, revenue, or anything that could identify a business.

post.description:
Marketing-site contact form. No auth, no DB write — the message is
relayed straight to the team inbox by email. Rate-limited per IP since
this is a public, unauthenticated, abuse-prone endpoint.

get.description: Target of the unsubscribe link in outgoing marketing email. The signed token IS the authorisation — no login.

Discount rules with optional search (name or code), status and type filters, and each rule's real usage:
how many sales it was applied to and the discount it granted.
One rule with its usage summary and its campaign name.
The sales this rule was actually applied to: sale reference, date, branch, customer (with contacts:read) and amount.
Created, edited, activated, paused and archived events for this rule, from the audit log.

AdminResetPasswordRequest.title: AdminResetPasswordRequest
AdminResetPasswordRequest.description:
An administrator resetting someone else's password: to one they choose (to hand over in person when email does not
arrive), or, without one, to a generated one that is emailed and never returned.

CustomerCreateStrict.title: CustomerCreateStrict
CustomerCreateStrict.description:
A customer entered on the Customers page must carry a TIN, individual or business: receipts and invoices cite it.
The till (`source="pos"`) may add a buyer without one so a sale is never held up; the TIN can be added later.

DebtWriteOffRequest.title: DebtWriteOffRequest
DebtWriteOffRequest.description: `amount` is in the debt's own currency; leave it out to write off everything still outstanding.

FeatureOverrideUpdate.title: FeatureOverrideUpdate
FeatureOverrideUpdate.description:
Per-tenant feature overrides. The map is authoritative: keys set to their
catalog default are dropped, replacing the tenant's full override set.

MyProfileUpdate.title: MyProfileUpdate
MyProfileUpdate.description:
Self-service profile edits. Deliberately narrower than UserUpdate —
email, role, status and org assignment are administrator decisions, so
they are not reachable here even if a client sends them.

OrderBulkLine.title: OrderBulkLine
OrderBulkLine.description:
One line of a CSV order import. Lines sharing the same `order_reference`
are grouped into a single order (client_order_id), so multi-item orders are
one reference repeated. `status` defaults to Completed — importing historical
sales as Completed deducts stock and posts them to accounting exactly like a
POS sale; use Pending to record rows without touching stock or the ledger.

OrderCorrection.title: OrderCorrection
OrderCorrection.description: An owner's correction of a completed sale: the full set of lines it should have had, and why.

OrderDecision.title: OrderDecision
OrderDecision.description: Body of the approve / reject endpoints.

OrderPaymentEntry.title: OrderPaymentEntry
OrderPaymentEntry.description: One payment taken at checkout. A sale paid with several methods (a split) sends one entry per method; the sale is still recorded once.

ProductBulkLine.title: ProductBulkLine
ProductBulkLine.description:
One row of a product import. `batch_number` is optional — when given,
an InventoryBatch is created alongside the product (quantity = this row's
stock, unit_cost = this row's cost), so pharmacy/cosmetics imports can
carry expiry/lot tracking from the same spreadsheet instead of a second
manual step.

auto_ack_text.title: Auto Ack Text
auto_ack_text.default: Thanks for contacting Pesaa support. We've received your message and will reply shortly.

after_hours_text.title: After Hours Text
after_hours_text.default: Thanks for contacting Pesaa support. We're outside business hours right now and will reply on the next working day.

tax_type.description: vat | paye | withholding | consumption | corporate | personal_income

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name for the tax type

TenantLimitsUpdate.title: TenantLimitsUpdate
TenantLimitsUpdate.description: Usage quotas. None removes the limit (unlimited).

VatClassification.title: VatClassification
VatClassification.description: Classify many products at once (Product Management bulk action).
